title: Ocean Acidification
text: Ocean acidification is the ongoing process of decreasing pH in the Earth's oceans, caused by the absorption of carbon dioxide from the atmosphere. Since the Industrial Revolution, ocean pH has decreased from about 8.2 to 8.1 — a 26% increase in acidity. CO2 reacts with seawater to form carbonic acid, which dissociates to bicarbonate and hydrogen ions. The increase in hydrogen ions reduces the carbonate ion concentration, making it harder for marine organisms like corals, mollusks, and echinoderms to form calcium carbonate shells and skeletons. Ocean acidification threatens marine biodiversity and fisheries that billions of people depend on for food and livelihood.
